# Broad sense heritability calculations

## Raw dataset

```{r}
data250pisum_00 <- read.csv("../../../../../../01.data/2023_screen_specifics_251genotypes/01.acyrthosiphon_pisum_P123amp_on_faba_collection/acyrthospipon_pisum_fecundity_on_faba_collection.csv", 
                            stringsAsFactors = FALSE, 
                            sep = ",") %>%  
  mutate(ivip = as.factor(ivip)) %>% 
  mutate(session = as.factor(session)) 

res <- calculate_broad_heritability(data = data250pisum_00)
```

::: callout-tip
Conclusions:\
- Heritability is equal to `r round(res$heritability, digits=3)`.\
- There are `r res$number_of_genotypes` genotypes in total.\
- There are `r res$number_of_notation` measurements in total.
:::
we can't use our dataset like this, we need to clean it first.

## Missing data removed
First we remove the missing data
```{r}
data250pisum_01 <- data250pisum_00 %>% filter(!is.na(larvae_total_number))
data250pisum_01$ivip <- droplevels(data250pisum_01$ivip)

res2 <- calculate_broad_heritability(data = data250pisum_01)
```

\newpage

::: callout-tip
Conclusions:\
- Heritability is equal to `r round(res2$heritability, digits=3)`.\
- There are `r res2$number_of_genotypes` genotypes in total.\
- There are `r res2$number_of_notation` measurements in total.
:::

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true

create_correlation_plot(data = data250pisum_01,
                        group_cols = c("ivip", "session"),
                        value_col = "larvae_total_number")
```


## Remove observations with no adult alive

We chose to remove all data from plants on which no adult aphid was found. This decision was made to get rid of larvae installation bias and only assess the reproduction ability of the aphid.

When the adult aphid dies, the number of larvae will drop but only because the adult did not stay much time on the plant and not because the plant was not suitable for the reproduction.

```{r remove observations with adult not alive}

data250pisum_02<- data250pisum_01 %>% filter(adult_alive != "0") 
data250pisum_02$ivip <- droplevels(data250pisum_02$ivip)

res3 <- calculate_broad_heritability(data = data250pisum_02)
```

::: callout-tip
Conclusions:\
- Heritability is equal to `r round(res3$heritability, digits=3)`.\
- There are `r res3$number_of_genotypes` genotypes in total.\
- There are `r res3$number_of_notation` measurements in total.
:::

This filtering led to the loss of 1 genotype but increased broad sense heritability up to 0.37

```{r}
#| eval: false

# Call the function to generate and display the correlation plot
create_correlation_plot(data250pisum_02, 
                         group_cols = c("ivip", "session"), 
                         value_col = "larvae_total_number")
```

Distribution normality check. 
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 8

p_with <- data250pisum_02 %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(sample=larvae_total_number)) +
  stat_qq() +
  stat_qq_line() +
  labs(y = "Observed quantiles", x = "Theoretical quantiles") +
  ggtitle("With outliers") +
  theme_bw()
p_with
```
## Filter outliers 
Our data are still not normally distributed. We need to apply a new filter. To remove outliers we choose to use the interquartile range method (IQR) removing data that are considered too high or too low. Both case can be explained biologically, low larvae count may be explain by an adult that was hurt during the installation and a larvae count too high may be explained by 2 adult beeing installed on the plant instead of only one.

```{r comparison of qqplots with and without outliers}

IQR_value <- IQR(data250pisum_02$larvae_total_number)
lower_bound <- quantile(data250pisum_02$larvae_total_number, 0.25) - 1.5 * IQR_value
upper_bound <- quantile(data250pisum_02$larvae_total_number, 0.75) + 1.5 * IQR_value

# Filter out outliers
data250pisum_03 <- data250pisum_02[data250pisum_02$larvae_total_number >= lower_bound & data250pisum_02$larvae_total_number <= upper_bound, ]

# Identify the rows that were removed (outliers)
removed_outliers <- data250pisum_02[data250pisum_02$larvae_total_number < lower_bound | data250pisum_02$larvae_total_number > upper_bound, ]

res4 <- calculate_broad_heritability(data = data250pisum_03)

#| fig-width: 8

# Without outliers
p_without <- data250pisum_03 %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(sample=larvae_total_number)) +
  stat_qq() +
  stat_qq_line() +
  labs(y = "Observed quantiles", x = "Theoretical quantiles") +
  ggtitle("Without outliers") +
  theme_bw()


p_with + p_without

```
::: callout-tip
Conclusions:\
- Heritability is equal to `r round(res4$heritability, digits=3)`.\
- There are `r res4$number_of_genotypes` genotypes in total.\
- There are `r res4$number_of_notation` measurements in total.
:::
 Both the normality of the data and the heritability benefits from this filter.
 
\newpage


# Final filtering: keep genotypes with at least 4/5/6 biological repetitions

```{r}
data250pisum_04_4 <- data250pisum_03 %>%
  group_by(ivip) %>%           # Group by genotype
  filter(n() >= 4) %>%             # Keep only groups with 4 or more repetitions
  ungroup()  
data250pisum_04_4$ivip <- droplevels(data250pisum_04_4$ivip)
res5 <- calculate_broad_heritability(data = data250pisum_04_4)
```


```{r}
data250pisum_04_5 <- data250pisum_03 %>%
  group_by(ivip) %>%           # Group by genotype
  filter(n() >= 5) %>%             # Keep only groups with 5 or more repetitions
  ungroup()  
data250pisum_04_5$ivip_5 <- droplevels(data250pisum_04_5$ivip)
res5 <- calculate_broad_heritability(data = data250pisum_04_5)
```

```{r}
data250pisum_04_6 <- data250pisum_03 %>%
  group_by(ivip) %>%           # Group by genotype
  filter(n() >= 6) %>%             # Keep only groups with 6 or more repetitions
  ungroup()  
data250pisum_04_6$ivip <- droplevels(data250pisum_04_6$ivip)
res5 <- calculate_broad_heritability(data = data250pisum_04_6)
```

::: callout-important
Conclusions:\
- Heritability is equal to `r round(res5$heritability, digits=3)`.\
- There are `r res5$number_of_genotypes` genotypes in total.\
- There are `r res5$number_of_notation` measurements in total.
:::

```{r}
#| eval: false
cor<-create_correlation_plot(data250pisum_04_6, 
                         group_cols = c("genotype", "session"), 
                         value_col = "larvae_total_number")
cortable<-cor$corrPos
mean(cortable$corr)
sd(cortable$corr)
mean(cortable$corr[cortable$p.value < 0.1], na.rm = TRUE)
sd(cortable$corr[cortable$p.value < 0.1], na.rm = TRUE)

```


```{r}
mod_h2 <- lmer(larvae_total_number ~ (1 | ivip) + (1 | session), data = data250pisum_04_6)
  estimates <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(mod_h2))
  genetic_variance <- estimates$vcov[1]
  residual_variance <- estimates$vcov[3]
  nbE <- nlevels(data250pisum_04_6$session)
  H2 <- genetic_variance / (genetic_variance + (residual_variance / nbE))
```
